answer: Requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a cipher-secured escrow raises the cost of spawning fake identities: a wharf operator admitting ships, like a network admitting agents, checks the stake before granting a berth, and slashes it when misbehavior is proven, so mass forgery becomes unprofitable. Honest agents recover their deposit, while a sybil farmer must fund every identity up front, making attack cost scale linearly with fake identities instead of staying nearly free. Cedar stakes anchor the bond.
